q: We ________ our friend's birthday and we ________ how to make it up to him.
exp:
Adverb 'completely' verb se pehle natural lagta hai: 'completely forgot'.
'just' ka sahi position: 'we just don't know' (matlab bilkul pata nahi).
'don't just know' ka meaning badal jaata hai (sirf jaante nahi, aur bhi...), jo yahan fit nahi.
Isliye: completely forgot --- just don't know.
Answer: (C)

q: Choose the statement where underlined word is used correctly. (underlined word: personnel)
opts: The industrialist had a personnel jet.
I write my experience in my personnel diary.
All personnel are being given the day off.
Being religious is a personnel aspect.
exp:
'personnel' = kisi organisation ke employees / staff (noun).
'personal' = vyaktigat / apna (adjective).
(A), (B), (D) me 'personal' hona chahiye tha (personal jet, personal diary, personal aspect).
(C) 'All personnel are being given the day off' = saare employees ko chhutti - sahi usage.
Answer: (C)

q: A generic term that includes various items of clothing such as a skirt, a pair of trousers and a shirt is
exp:
Fabric / textile = kapda (cloth material), fibre = dhaaga banane wala raw material.
Skirt, trousers, shirt - ye sab pehne jaane wale kapde hain, unka generic term 'apparel' hai.
Answer: (D)

q:
Based on the given statements, select the most appropriate option to solve the given question.

What will be the total weight of 10 poles each of same weight?

Statements:
(I) One fourth of the weight of a pole is 5 Kg.
(II) The total weight of these poles is 160 kg more than the total weight of two poles.
opts: Statement I alone is not sufficient.
Statement II alone is not sufficient.
Either I or II alone is sufficient.
Both statements I and II together are not sufficient.
exp:
Statement I: w/4 = 5 => w = 20 kg => 10 poles = 200 kg. Sufficient.
Statement II: 10w = 2w + 160 => 8w = 160 => w = 20 kg => 200 kg. Sufficient.
Dono me se koi bhi ek akela kaafi hai.
Answer: (C)

q: Consider a function f(x) = 1 − |x| on −1 ≤ x ≤ 1. The value of x at which the function attains a maximum, and the maximum value of the function are:
exp:
|x| ≥ 0 hota hai, toh f(x) = 1 − |x| tab maximum jab |x| minimum = 0, yaani x = 0.
f(0) = 1 − 0 = 1.
Endpoints par f(±1) = 0, jo chhota hai.
Toh x = 0 par max value 1.
Answer: (C)

q: Out of the following four sentences, select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage:
opts: Since the report lacked needed information, it was of no use to them.
The report was useless to them because there were no needed information in it.
Since the report did not contain the needed information, it was not real useful to them.
Since the report lacked needed information, it would not had been useful to them.
exp:
(B) 'information' uncountable hai => 'there was', 'there were' galat.
(C) 'real useful' galat - adverb chahiye 'really useful'.
(D) 'would not had been' galat - sahi form 'would not have been'.
(A) grammatically bilkul sahi hai.
Answer: (A)

q:
In a triangle PQR, PS is the angle bisector of ∠QPR and ∠QPS = 60°. What is the length of PS?
(Figure: triangle PQR with S on side QR; PQ = r, PR = q, QR = p.)
exp:
PS bisector hai aur ∠QPS = 60° => ∠QPR = 120°, ∠RPS = 60°.
Area(PQR) = Area(PQS) + Area(PRS).
½·q·r·sin120° = ½·r·PS·sin60° + ½·q·PS·sin60°.
sin120° = sin60°, cancel karo: qr = PS(q + r).
PS = qr/(q + r).
Answer: (B)

q:
If p, q, r, s are distinct integers such that:
f(p, q, r, s) = max(p, q, r, s)
g(p, q, r, s) = min(p, q, r, s)
h(p, q, r, s) = remainder of (p × q) / (r × s) if (p × q) > (r × s) or remainder of (r × s) / (p × q) if (r × s) > (p × q)

Also a function fgh(p, q, r, s) = f(p, q, r, s) × g(p, q, r, s) × h(p, q, r, s)
Also the same operations are valid with two variable functions of the form f(p, q).
What is the value of fg(h(2,5,7,3), 4,6,8)?
exp:
Pehle h(2,5,7,3): p×q = 10, r×s = 21.
21 > 10, toh remainder of 21/10 = 1.
Ab fg(1, 4, 6, 8) = f × g = max × min.
max(1,4,6,8) = 8, min = 1.
fg = 8 × 1 = 8.
Answer: 8

q:
If the list of letters, P, R, S, T, U is an arithmetic sequence, which of the following are also in arithmetic sequence?
I. 2P, 2R, 2S, 2T, 2U
II. P−3, R−3, S−3, T−3, U−3
III. P², R², S², T², U²
exp:
AP ke har term ko constant se multiply karo => common difference 2d, phir bhi AP. I sahi.
Har term se constant subtract karo => difference d same, AP. II sahi.
Squares: e.g. 1,2,3 -> 1,4,9, differences 3,5 - AP nahi. III galat.
Answer: (B)

q: Four branches of a company are located at M, N, O, and P. M is north of N at a distance of 4 km; P is south of O at a distance of 2 km; N is southeast of O by 1 km. What is the distance between M and P in km?

Consider the following two statements.
S1: If a candidate is known to be corrupt, then he will not be elected
S2: If a candidate is kind, he will be elected
Which one of the following statements follows from S1 and S2 as per sound inference rules of logic?
opts: If a person is known to be corrupt, he is kind
If a person is not known to be corrupt, he is not kind
If a person is kind, he is not known to be corrupt
If a person is not kind, he is not known to be corrupt
exp:
S1: C → ¬E, S2: K → E.
S1 ka contrapositive: E → ¬C.
Chain (hypothetical syllogism): K → E → ¬C, toh K → ¬C.
Matlab: agar kind hai toh known to be corrupt nahi hai.
Trap: (D) inverse hai (¬K → ¬C), wo follow nahi karta.
Answer: (C)

q: The cardinality of the power set of {0, 1, 2, ..., 10} is ______.
exp:
Set {0,1,...,10} me 11 elements hain (0 ko count karna mat bhoolo).
|P(S)| = 2ⁿ = 2¹¹ = 2048.
Trap: 10 elements samajh ke 1024 likhna.
Answer: 2048

q: Let R be the relation on the set of positive integers such that aRb if and only if a and b are distinct and have a common divisor other than 1. Which one of the following statements about R is true?
opts: R is symmetric and reflexive but not transitive
R is reflexive but not symmetric and not transitive
R is transitive but not reflexive and not symmetric
R is symmetric but not reflexive and not transitive
exp:
Reflexive: aRa ke liye a, a distinct hone chahiye - impossible. Not reflexive.
Symmetric: gcd(a,b) > 1 aur a ≠ b => b, a ke liye bhi same. Symmetric.
Transitive: 2R6 (gcd 2), 6R3 (gcd 3), par 2R3? gcd = 1 => nahi. Not transitive.
Answer: (D)

q: The number of divisors of 2100 is ______.
exp:
Prime factorisation: 2100 = 2² × 3¹ × 5² × 7¹.
Divisors count = (2+1)(1+1)(2+1)(1+1).
= 3 × 2 × 3 × 2 = 36.
Answer: 36

q: The larger of the two eigenvalues of the matrix [[4, 5], [2, 1]] is ______.
exp:
Characteristic equation: λ² − (trace)λ + det = 0.
Trace = 4 + 1 = 5, det = 4·1 − 5·2 = −6.
λ² − 5λ − 6 = 0 => (λ − 6)(λ + 1) = 0.
λ = 6, −1. Larger = 6.
Answer: 6

q: An unordered list contains n distinct elements. The number of comparisons to find an element in this list that is neither maximum nor minimum is
exp:
Koi bhi 3 distinct elements utha lo (e.g. pehle 3).
In teeno ka middle element puri list ka na max ho sakta hai na min (ek bada aur ek chhota exist karta hai).
3 elements ka middle nikalne me max 3 comparisons - constant.
Trap: poori list ka max/min nikalne ki zaroorat nahi.
Answer: (D) Θ(1)

q: The minimum number of JK flip-flops required to construct a synchronous counter with the count sequence (0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,0,0,...) is ______.
exp:
Sequence me har value do baar aati hai: 0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3 - total 8 distinct states chahiye.
Kyunki pehla '0' aur doosra '0' ke next states alag hain (0 aur 1), dono ko alag state hona padega.
8 states ke liye ⌈log₂8⌉ = 3 flip-flops.
Trap: sirf 4 values dekh ke 2 FF bolna.
Answer: 3

q: Assume that for a certain processor, a read request takes 50 nanoseconds on a cache miss and 5 nanoseconds on a cache hit. Suppose while running a program, it was observed that 80% of the processor's read requests result in a cache hit. The average read access time in nanoseconds is ______.
exp:
Hit ratio h = 0.8, hit time = 5 ns, miss time = 50 ns (total).
Avg = h × 5 + (1 − h) × 50.
= 0.8 × 5 + 0.2 × 50 = 4 + 10 = 14 ns.
Answer: 14

q: A computer system implements a 40-bit virtual address, page size of 8 kilobytes, and a 128-entry translation look-aside buffer (TLB) organized into 32 sets each having four ways. Assume that the TLB tag does not store any process id. The minimum length of the TLB tag in bits is ______.
exp:
Page size 8 KB = 2¹³ => offset 13 bits.
VPN = 40 − 13 = 27 bits.
TLB 32 sets => set index = log₂32 = 5 bits (VPN se liye jaate hain).
Tag = VPN − index = 27 − 5 = 22 bits.
Answer: 22

q:
Consider the following statements.
I. The complement of every Turing decidable language is Turing decidable
II. There exists some language which is in NP but is not Turing decidable
III. If L is a language in NP, L is Turing decidable
Which of the above statements is/are true?
exp:
I: Decidable languages complement ke under closed hain (accept/reject swap karo). True.
NP ka har language ek NTM se polynomial time me decide hota hai => decidable.
Toh II false, III true.
Answer: (D) Only I and III

q:
Consider the following function written in the C programming language.
The output of the above function on input "ABCD  EFGH" is
exp:
foo tab tak recurse karta hai jab tak *a non-null aur space nahi hai.
Pehle recursive call, phir putchar => characters reverse order me print honge.
String 'ABCD' ke baad space aata hai, wahan recursion ruk jaata hai.
Unwinding me print: D, C, B, A.
Trap: EFGH kabhi visit hi nahi hota.
Answer: (D) DCBA

q: Consider a complete binary tree where the left and the right subtrees of the root are max-heaps. The lower bound for the number of operations to convert the tree to a heap is
exp:
Dono subtrees already max-heap hain, sirf root galat position par ho sakta hai.
Ek baar max-heapify (sift-down) root par chalao.
Worst case root ko leaf tak jaana padta hai = height = log n.
Toh Θ(log n) operations, lower bound Ω(log n).
Answer: (A)

q: A binary tree T has 20 leaves. The number of nodes in T having two children is ______.
exp:
Kisi bhi binary tree me: n₀ = n₂ + 1 (leaves = degree-2 nodes + 1).
n₀ = 20 => n₂ = 19.
(Degree-1 nodes is relation ko affect nahi karte.)
Answer: 19

q:
Consider the following C function.
The return value of fun(5) is ______.
A software requirements specification (SRS) document should avoid discussing which one of the following?
exp:
SRS batata hai system 'kya' karega (WHAT), 'kaise' karega (HOW) nahi.
UI issues, non-functional requirements, external interfaces - ye sab requirements ka part hain.
Design specification implementation ka 'how' hai - wo design document me jaata hai.
Answer: (C)

q: Consider two decision problems Q₁, Q₂ such that Q₁ reduces in polynomial time to 3-SAT and 3-SAT reduces in polynomial time to Q₂. Then which one of the following is consistent with the above statement?
opts: Q₁ is in NP, Q₂ is NP hard.
Q₂ is in NP, Q₁ is NP hard.
Both Q₁ and Q₂ are in NP.
Both Q₁ and Q₂ are NP hard.
exp:
Q₁ ≤p 3-SAT aur 3-SAT ∈ NP => Q₁ ∈ NP (Q₁ utna hi easy hai).
3-SAT ≤p Q₂ aur 3-SAT NP-complete => Q₂ NP-hard hai.
Q₁ NP-hard hai ya nahi, pata nahi; Q₂ NP me hai ya nahi, pata nahi.
Answer: (A)

q:
Match the following:
P. Lexical analysis        1. Graph coloring
Q. Parsing                 2. DFA minimization
R. Register allocation     3. Post-order traversal
S. Expression evaluation   4. Production tree
exp:
Lexical analysis: tokens ke liye DFA banta hai, minimize kiya jaata hai => P-2.
Parsing: derivation / parse (production) tree => Q-4.
Register allocation: interference graph ka graph coloring => R-1.
Expression evaluation: expression tree ka post-order traversal => S-3.
Answer: (C)

q: In the context of abstract-syntax-tree (AST) and control-flow-graph (CFG), which one of the following is TRUE?
opts: In both AST and CFG, let node N₂ be the successor of node N₁. In the input program, the code corresponding to N₂ is present after the code corresponding to N₁
For any input program, neither AST nor CFG will contain a cycle
The maximum number of successors of a node in an AST and a CFG depends on the input program
Each node in AST and CFG corresponds to at most one statement in the input program
exp:
(A) galat: CFG me loop back-edge ka successor code me pehle hota hai.
(B) galat: loops ki wajah se CFG me cycle hoti hai.
(D) galat: CFG node = basic block, jisme kai statements ho sakte hain.
(C) sahi: AST me children count (e.g. function args) aur CFG me successors (switch cases) program par depend karte hain.
Answer: (C)

q: Consider the basic COCOMO model where E is the effort applied in person-months, D is the development time in chronological months, KLOC is the estimated number of delivered lines of code (in thousands) and a_b, b_b, c_b, d_b have their usual meanings. The basic COCOMO equations are of the form
opts: E = a_b(KLOC) exp(b_b), D = c_b(E) exp(d_b)
D = a_b(KLOC) exp(b_b), E = c_b(D) exp(d_b)
E = a_b exp(b_b), D = c_b(KLOC) exp(d_b)
E = a_b exp(d_b), D = c_b(KLOC) exp(b_b)
exp:
Basic COCOMO: Effort E = a_b × (KLOC)^b_b person-months.
Development time D = c_b × (E)^d_b months.
Yahan 'exp(x)' ka matlab 'power x' hai.
Effort KLOC se aata hai, time effort se.
Answer: (A)

q: A system has 6 identical resources and N processes competing for them. Each process can request atmost 2 resources. Which one of the following values of N could lead to a deadlock?
exp:
Idea: jitne zyada processes, utna zyada chance ki sab resources partially allocate ho jaayein aur har koi aur maange.
N = 1, 2, 3 me har process ko 2 resources ek saath mil sakte hain (2N ≤ 6) - deadlock possible hi nahi.
Official key ne sirf N = 4 ko deadlock-prone option maana hai (2N = 8 > 6, yaani saari demands ek saath satisfy nahi ho sakti).
Isliye options me se answer N = 4.
Trap: Strict formula N(max−1) + 1 ≤ 6 se N ≤ 5 tak deadlock-free aata hai; is wajah se ye question controversial raha, par official answer (D) hai.
Answer: (D)

q:
Consider the following transaction involving two bank accounts x and y.
read(x); x := x − 50; write(x); read(y); y := y + 50; write(y)
The constraint that the sum of the accounts x and y should remain constant is that of
exp:
Sum x + y constant rehna ek integrity constraint (database invariant) hai.
Transaction ek consistent state se doosri consistent state me le jaaye - yahi Consistency hai.
Atomicity = all or nothing, Isolation = concurrent interference nahi, Durability = commit ke baad permanent.
Answer: (B)

q:
With reference to the B+ tree index of order 1 shown below, the minimum number of nodes (including the Root node) that must be fetched in order to satisfy the following query: "Get all records with a search key greater than or equal to 7 and less than 15" is ______.

B+ tree:
Root: [9]
  Left child of root: [5]  -> leaves [1 | 3] and [5 | 7]
  Right child of root: [13 | 17] -> leaves [9 | 11], [13 | 15], [17 | _]
Leaves are linked left-to-right: [1|3] ↔ [5|7] ↔ [9|11] ↔ [13|15] ↔ [17|_]
exp:
Search key 7 se start: Root [9] fetch (1) -> 7 < 9, left child [5] (2) -> 7 ≥ 5, leaf [5|7] (3).
Ab leaf-chain par aage badho: leaf [9|11] (4) - dono keys range me.
Leaf [13|15] (5): 13 range me, 15 nahi (<15 chahiye) => yahin stop.
Total nodes = 5.
Answer: 5

q: Identify the correct order in which a server process must invoke the function calls accept, bind, listen, and recv according to UNIX socket API.
exp:
Server side sequence: socket() -> bind() (address/port attach) -> listen() (passive socket banao) -> accept() (client connection lo) -> recv() (data padho).
Answer: (B)

q: A link has a transmission speed of 10⁶ bits/sec. It uses data packets of size 1000 bytes each. Assume that the acknowledgment has negligible transmission delay, and that its propagation delay is the same as the data propagation delay. Also assume that the processing delays at nodes are negligible. The efficiency of the stop-and-wait protocol in this setup is exactly 25%. The value of the one-way propagation delay (in milliseconds) is ______.
exp:
Tt = 1000 × 8 / 10⁶ = 8 ms.
Stop-and-wait efficiency η = Tt / (Tt + 2Tp).
0.25 = 8 / (8 + 2Tp) => 8 + 2Tp = 32 => Tp = 12 ms.
Answer: 12

q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about HTTP cookies?
opts: A cookie is a piece of code that has the potential to compromise the security of an Internet user
A cookie gains entry to the user's work area through an HTTP header
A cookie has an expiry date and time
Cookies can be used to track the browsing pattern of a user at a particular site
exp:
Cookie ek chhota text data (name=value) hai, executable code nahi.
Server Set-Cookie HTTP header se bhejta hai - (B) sahi.
Cookie ka Expires/Max-Age hota hai - (C) sahi.
Tracking ke liye use hote hain - (D) sahi.
'Piece of code' kehna galat hai.
Answer: (A)

q:
Consider the following routing table at an IP router:
Network No.     Net Mask          Next Hop
128.96.170.0    255.255.254.0     Interface 0
128.96.168.0    255.255.254.0     Interface 1
128.96.166.0    255.255.254.0     R2
128.96.164.0    255.255.252.0     R3
0.0.0.0         Default           R4

For each IP address in Group I identify the correct choice of the next hop from Group II using the entries from the routing table above.
Group I: i) 128.96.171.92  ii) 128.96.167.151  iii) 128.96.163.151  iv) 128.96.165.121
Group II: a) Interface 0  b) Interface 1  c) R2  d) R3  e) R4
exp:
Third octet ko mask se AND karo (254 = 11111110, 252 = 11111100).
i) 171 AND 254 = 170 => 128.96.170.0 => Interface 0 (a).
ii) 167 AND 254 = 166 => R2 (c).
iii) 163 AND 254 = 162 (no match), 163 AND 252 = 160 ≠ 164 => default R4 (e).
iv) 165 AND 254 = 164 (koi /23 entry nahi), 165 AND 252 = 164 => R3 (d).
Answer: (A)

q: Host A sends a UDP datagram containing 8880 bytes of user data to host B over an Ethernet LAN. Ethernet frames may carry data up to 1500 bytes (i.e. MTU=1500 bytes). Size of UDP header is 8 bytes and size of IP header is 20 bytes. There is no option field in IP header. How many total number of IP fragments will be transmitted and what will be the contents of offset field in the last fragment?
exp:
IP payload = 8880 + 8 (UDP header) = 8888 bytes.
Har fragment me max data = 1500 − 20 = 1480 bytes (8 ka multiple ✓).
Fragments = ⌈8888 / 1480⌉ = ⌈6.005⌉ = 7 (6 full + last me 8 bytes).
Last fragment ka byte offset = 6 × 1480 = 8880; offset field 8-byte units me = 8880/8 = 1110.
Trap: UDP header ke 8 bytes add karna mat bhoolo.
Answer: (C)

q: Assume that the bandwidth for a TCP connection is 1048560 bits/sec. Let α be the value of RTT in milliseconds (rounded off to the nearest integer) after which the TCP window scale option is needed. Let β be the maximum possible window size with window scale option. Then the values of α and β are
exp:
Without scaling max window = 65535 bytes (16-bit field).
Pipe full karne ke liye window = BW × RTT. Scaling tab chahiye jab BW × RTT > 65535 × 8 bits.
RTT = 65535 × 8 / 1048560 = 524280 / 1048560 = 0.5 s = 500 ms => α = 500.
Window scale shift max 14 hota hai => β = 65535 × 2¹⁴.
Trap: shift 16 allowed nahi (RFC 1323 limit 14).
Answer: (C)

opts: Undo: T3, T1; Redo: T2, T4
Undo: none; Redo: T2, T4, T3, T1
Undo: T3, T1, T4; Redo: T2
exp:
T4 checkpoint se pehle commit ho chuka => uske changes disk par, kuch nahi karna.
T1 checkpoint se pehle start, commit nahi hua => Undo.
T2 checkpoint ke baad start aur commit => Redo.
T3 start hua, commit nahi => Undo.
Undo: T3, T1; Redo: T2.
Answer: (A)

q: Consider two relations R₁(A,B) with the tuples (1,5), (3,7) and R₂(A,C) = (1,7), (4,9). Assume that R(A,B,C) is the full natural outer join of R₁ and R₂. Consider the following tuples of the form (A,B,C): a = (1,5,null), b = (1,null,7), c = (3,null,9), d = (4,7,null), e = (1,5,7), f = (3,7,null), g = (4,null,9). Which one of the following statements is correct?
opts: R contains a, b, e, f, g but not c, d.
R contains all of a, b, c, d, e, f, g.
R contains e, f, g but not a, b.
R contains e but not f, g.
exp:
Common attribute A par join.
A = 1 dono me hai => (1, 5, 7) = e.
A = 3 sirf R₁ me => (3, 7, null) = f.
A = 4 sirf R₂ me => (4, null, 9) = g.
R = {e, f, g}; a, b nahi hain.
Answer: (C)

q: Consider six memory partitions of sizes 200 KB, 400 KB, 600 KB, 500 KB, 300 KB and 250 KB, where KB refers to kilobyte. These partitions need to be allotted to four processes of sizes 357 KB, 210 KB, 468 KB and 491 KB in that order. If the best fit algorithm is used, which partitions are NOT allotted to any process?
exp:
Best fit = sabse chhota partition jisme process fit ho.
357 KB -> 400 KB.
210 KB -> 250 KB.
468 KB -> 500 KB.
491 KB -> 600 KB.
Bache: 200 KB aur 300 KB.
Answer: (A)

q: Consider a typical disk that rotates at 15000 rotations per minute (RPM) and has a transfer rate of 50×10⁶ bytes/sec. If the average seek time of the disk is twice the average rotational delay and the controller's transfer time is 10 times the disk transfer time, the average time (in milliseconds) to read or write a 512-byte sector of the disk is ______.
exp:
15000 RPM => 1 rotation = 60/15000 s = 4 ms. Avg rotational delay = 2 ms.
Avg seek = 2 × 2 = 4 ms.
Disk transfer time = 512 / (50×10⁶) s = 10.24 µs = 0.01024 ms.
Controller time = 10 × 0.01024 = 0.1024 ms.
Total = 4 + 2 + 0.01024 + 0.1024 ≈ 6.11 ms.
Answer: ≈ 6.11 (range 6.1 to 6.2)

q: A computer system implements 8 kilobyte pages and a 32-bit physical address space. Each page table entry contains a valid bit, a dirty bit, three permission bits, and the translation. If the maximum size of the page table of a process is 24 megabytes, the length of the virtual address supported by the system is ______ bits.
exp:
Page size 8 KB => offset 13 bits. Frame number = 32 − 13 = 19 bits.
PTE = 19 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 24 bits = 3 bytes.
Entries = 24 MB / 3 B = 8M = 2²³.
Virtual address = 23 (page no.) + 13 (offset) = 36 bits.
Answer: 36

q:
Consider the intermediate code given below.
(1) i = 1
(2) j = 1
(3) t1 = 5 * i
(4) t2 = t1 + j
(5) t3 = 4 * t2
(6) t4 = t3
(7) a[t4] = -1
(8) j = j + 1
(9) if j<=5 goto (3)
(10) i=i+1
(11) if i<5 goto (2)
The number of nodes and edges in the control-flow-graph constructed for the above code, respectively, are
exp:
Leaders: (1) first stmt, (2) aur (3) jump targets, (10) jump ke baad wala stmt.
Blocks: B1 = {1}, B2 = {2}, B3 = {3..9}, B4 = {10, 11}.
Entry aur Exit node add karo => 6 nodes.
Edges: Entry→B1, B1→B2, B2→B3, B3→B3 (loop), B3→B4, B4→B2, B4→Exit = 7.
Answer: (B) 6 and 7

q: The number of states in the minimal deterministic finite automaton corresponding to the regular expression (0 + 1)*(10) is ______.
exp:
Language = '10' se end hone wali strings.
States: q0 (koi useful suffix nahi), q1 (last symbol 1), q2 (last two '10', final).
q0: 0→q0, 1→q1; q1: 0→q2, 1→q1; q2: 0→q0, 1→q1.
Teeno distinguishable => minimal DFA me 3 states.
Answer: 3

L₁: w ko single symbol le lo, baaki x me absorb => strings jo same symbol se start aur end karein, length ≥ 3: a(a+b)⁺a + b(a+b)⁺b. Regular.
L₂: m ≠ n ke liye count compare karna padta hai - not regular (complement ∩ a*b* = aⁿbⁿ).
L₃ = a*b*c* - regular.
Trap: wxwᴿ dekh ke palindrome samajh kar non-regular bolna.
Answer: (A)

q:
Given below are some algorithms, and some algorithm design paradigms.
1. Dijkstra's Shortest Path
2. Floyd-Warshall algorithm to compute all pairs shortest path
3. Binary search on a sorted array
4. Backtracking search on a graph

i. Divide and Conquer
ii. Dynamic Programming
iii. Greedy design
iv. Depth-first search
v. Breadth-first search

Match the above algorithms on the left to the corresponding design paradigm they follow.
exp:
Dijkstra: har step par min-distance vertex choose karta hai => Greedy (iii).
Floyd-Warshall: D^k[i][j] = min(D^(k−1)[i][j], D^(k−1)[i][k] + D^(k−1)[k][j]) => DP (ii).
Binary search => Divide and Conquer (i).
Backtracking => depth-first exploration (iv).
Answer: (C)

q:
A Young tableau is a 2D array of integers increasing from left to right and from top to bottom. Any unfilled entries are marked with ∞, and hence there cannot be any entry to the right of, or below a ∞. The following Young tableau consists of unique entries.
1   2   5   14
3   4   6   23
10  12  18  25
31  ∞   ∞   ∞
When an element is removed from a Young tableau, other elements should be moved into its place so that the resulting table is still a Young tableau (unfilled entries may be filled in with a ∞). The minimum number of entries (other than 1) to be shifted, to remove 1 from the given Young tableau is ______.
exp:
1 hatao => (0,0) khali. Har step par right aur neeche wale me se chhota element hole me laao.
(0,0): right 2, down 3 => 2 left shift. Hole (0,1).
(0,1): right 5, down 4 => 4 upar. Hole (1,1).
(1,1): right 6, down 12 => 6 left. Hole (1,2).
(1,2): right 23, down 18 => 18 upar. Hole (2,2).
(2,2): right 25, down ∞ => 25 left. Hole (2,3), iske right/neeche kuch nahi => ∞ bharo.
Shifted: 2, 4, 6, 18, 25 = 5.
Answer: 5

q:
Suppose you are provided with the following function declaration in the C programming language.
    int partition(int a[], int n);
The function treats the first element of a[] as a pivot, and rearranges the array so that all elements less than or equal to the pivot is in the left part of the array, and all elements greater than the pivot is in the right part. In addition, it moves the pivot so that the pivot is the last element of the left part. The return value is the number of elements in the left part.
The following partially given function in the C programming language is used to find the kth smallest element in an array a[] of size n using the partition function. We assume k ≤ n.
The missing argument lists are respectively
exp:
Code ke hisaab se pivot index left_end par hai (a[left_end] return hota hai jab left_end+1 == k).
Agar left_end+1 > k: answer pivot se pehle wale left_end elements me hai => kth_smallest(a, left_end, k).
Warna right part me: start a+left_end+1, size n−left_end−1, aur k me se left_end+1 elements (pivot sahit) ghatao => k−left_end−1.
Answer: (A)

q: Which one of the following hash functions on integers will distribute keys most uniformly over 10 buckets numbered 0 to 9 for i ranging from 0 to 2020?
exp:
Last digit ke hisaab se socho (i mod 10 = 0..9).
i² mod 10: {0,1,4,9,6,5,6,9,4,1} - sirf 0,1,4,5,6,9 aate hain. (C) bhi same (11i² ≡ i²).
12i mod 10 = 2i mod 10 - sirf even digits.
i³ mod 10: {0,1,8,7,4,5,6,3,2,9} - saare 10 digits, one-to-one => uniform.
Answer: (B)

q: The secant method is used to find the root of an equation f(x) = 0. It is started from two distinct estimates xₐ and x_b for the root. It is an iterative procedure involving linear interpolation to a root. The iteration stops if f(x_b) is very small and then x_b is the solution. The procedure is given below. Observe that there is an expression which is missing and is marked by ?. Which is the suitable expression that is to be put in place of ? so that it follows all steps of the secant method?
code:
Secant
Initialize: xa, xb, ε, N      // ε = convergence indicator
                              // N = maximum no. of iterations
    fb = f(xb)
    i = 0
    while (i < N and |fb| > ε) do
        i = i + 1                 // update counter
        xt = ?                    // missing expression for
                                  // intermediate value
        xa = xb                   // reset xa
        xb = xt                   // reset xb
        fb = f(xb)                // function value at new xb
    end while
    if |fb| > ε then              // loop is terminated with i=N
        write "Non-convergence"
    else
        write "return xb"
    end if
exp:
Secant formula: x_new = x_b − f(x_b) × (x_b − xₐ) / (f(x_b) − f(xₐ)).
Ye (xₐ, fₐ) aur (x_b, f_b) ko jodne wali line ka x-axis intercept hai.
Code me f_b = f(x_b), toh x_t = x_b − (x_b − xₐ) f_b / (f_b − f(xₐ)).
(A) me slope ulta hai (inverse), galat.
Answer: (C)

q:
Consider the C program below.
The value printed by the above program is ______.
exp:
stkFunc ke andar 'static int stkTop' local hai - wo global stkTop (= −1) ko shadow karta hai; local stkTop = 0 se start.

q:
Consider the sequence of machine instructions given below:
MUL R5, R0, R1
DIV R6, R2, R3
ADD R7, R5, R6
SUB R8, R7, R4
In the above sequence, R0 to R8 are general purpose registers. In the instructions shown, the first register stores the result of the operation performed on the second and the third registers. This sequence of instructions is to be executed in a pipelined instruction processor with the following 4 stages: (1) Instruction Fetch and Decode (IF), (2) Operand Fetch (OF), (3) Perform Operation (PO) and (4) Write back the result (WB). The IF, OF and WB stages take 1 clock cycle each for any instruction. The PO stage takes 1 clock cycle for ADD or SUB instruction, 3 clock cycles for MUL instruction and 5 clock cycles for DIV instruction. The pipelined processor uses operand forwarding from the PO stage to the OF stage. The number of clock cycles taken for the execution of the above sequence of instructions is ______.
exp:
MUL: IF 1, OF 2, PO 3–5, WB 6.
DIV: IF 2, OF 3, PO 6–10 (PO unit 5 tak busy), WB 11.
ADD (R6 DIV se chahiye): IF 3, OF 4, DIV ka result cycle 10 ke end par forward => PO 11, WB 12.
SUB (R7 ADD se): IF 4, OF 5, forwarding ke saath PO 12, WB 13.
Total = 13 cycles.
Answer: 13

q:
Consider a processor with byte-addressable memory. Assume that all registers, including Program Counter (PC) and Program Status Word (PSW), are of size 2 bytes. A stack in the main memory is implemented from memory location (0100)₁₆ and it grows upward. The stack pointer (SP) points to the top element of the stack. The current value of SP is (016E)₁₆. The CALL instruction is of two words, the first word is the op-code and the second word is the starting address of the subroutine (one word = 2 bytes). The CALL instruction is implemented as follows:
• Store the current value of PC in the stack
• Store the value of PSW register in the stack
• Load the starting address of the subroutine in PC
The content of PC just before the fetch of a CALL instruction is (5FA0)₁₆. After execution of the CALL instruction, the value of the stack pointer is
exp:
Stack upward grow karta hai, SP top element ko point karta hai.
PC (2 bytes) push: SP = 016E + 2 = 0170.
PSW (2 bytes) push: SP = 0170 + 2 = 0172.
(PC ki value 5FA4 store hogi, par SP par iska asar nahi.)
Answer: (D) (0172)₁₆

q:
The number of min-terms after minimizing the following Boolean expression is ______.
[D' + AB' + A'C + AC'D + A'C'D]'
exp:
Pehle andar wala G = D' + AB' + A'C + AC'D + A'C'D simplify karo.
D = 0 par D' = 1 => G = 1.
D = 1 par G = AB' + A'C + AC' + A'C' = AB' + A' + AC' = A' + B' + C'.
Toh G = 0 sirf jab A = B = C = D = 1.
F = G' = ABCD => sirf 1 minterm (m15).
Answer: 1

q:
Let f(x) = x^(−1/3) and A denote the area of the region bounded by f(x) and the X-axis, when x varies from −1 to 1. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
I) f is continuous in [−1, 1]
II) f is not bounded in [−1, 1]
III) A is nonzero and finite
exp:
x = 0 par f(x) = 1/x^(1/3) defined nahi, aur x → 0 par ±∞ => continuous nahi (I false), unbounded (II true).
Area = ∫|f| = 2 ∫₀¹ x^(−1/3) dx = 2 × [ (3/2) x^(2/3) ]₀¹ = 2 × 3/2 = 3.
Area nonzero aur finite => III true.
Answer: (C)

q:
Perform the following operations on the matrix
[[3, 4, 45], [7, 9, 105], [13, 2, 195]]
(i) Add the third row to the second row
(ii) Subtract the third column from the first column.
The determinant of the resultant matrix is ______.
exp:
Dekho: column 3 = 15 × column 1 (45 = 15·3, 105 = 15·7, 195 = 15·13).
Toh original det = 0 (columns linearly dependent).
Row ko doosri row me add karna aur column ko subtract karna - dono elementary operations determinant nahi badalte.
Resultant det = 0.
Answer: 0

q: The number of onto functions (surjective functions) from set X = {1, 2, 3, 4} to set Y = {a, b, c} is ______.
exp:
Inclusion–exclusion: onto = 3⁴ − C(3,1)·2⁴ + C(3,2)·1⁴.
= 81 − 48 + 3 = 36.
Check: 4 elements ko 3 non-empty groups me baanto = S(4,3) = 6, phir 3! = 6 se assign => 36.
Answer: 36

q: Let X and Y denote the sets containing 2 and 20 distinct objects respectively and F denote the set of all possible functions defined from X to Y. Let f be randomly chosen from F. The probability of f being one-to-one is ______.
exp:
Total functions = 20² = 400.
One-to-one functions = 20 × 19 = 380.
Probability = 380 / 400 = 0.95.
Answer: 0.95

q:
Consider the alphabet Σ = {0, 1}, the null/empty string λ and the sets of strings X₀, X₁, and X₂ generated by the corresponding non-terminals of a regular grammar. X₀, X₁, and X₂ are related as follows.
X₀ = 1 X₁
X₁ = 0 X₁ + 1 X₂
X₂ = 0 X₁ + {λ}
Which one of the following choices precisely represents the strings in X₀?
exp:
X₂ ko X₁ me substitute karo: X₁ = 0X₁ + 1(0X₁ + λ) = (0 + 10)X₁ + 1.
Arden's rule (X = PX + Q => X = P*Q): X₁ = (0 + 10)*1.
X₀ = 1X₁ = 1(0 + 10)*1.
Trap: (B) me '10' se start force hota hai, '11' miss ho jaata hai.
Answer: (C)

q: A graph is self-complementary if it is isomorphic to its complement. For all self-complementary graphs on n vertices, n is
exp:
Self-complementary => G aur G' ke edges barabar: |E| = n(n−1)/4.
Isliye n(n−1) ko 4 se divisible hona chahiye.
n aur n−1 me se ek hi even hai, toh ya n ≡ 0 (mod 4) ya n − 1 ≡ 0 (mod 4).
Examples: P₄ (n = 4), C₅ (n = 5).
Answer: (D)

q: In a connected graph, a bridge is an edge whose removal disconnects a graph. Which one of the following statements is true?
opts: A bridge cannot be part of a simple cycle
Every edge of a clique with size ≥ 3 is a bridge (A clique is any complete subgraph of a graph)
A graph with bridges cannot have a cycle
exp:
(A) galat: tree ki har edge bridge hai.
(B) sahi: agar edge cycle me hai toh uske endpoints cycle ke baaki path se connected rehte hain - removal se disconnect nahi.
(C) galat: clique (≥3) ki har edge ek triangle me hai, isliye bridge nahi.
(D) galat: ek cycle + ek pendant edge wale graph me bridge bhi hai aur cycle bhi.
Answer: (B)

q: Which one of the following well formed formulae is a tautology?
opts: (∀x [∃y R(x, y) → S(x, y)]) → ∀x∃y S(x, y)
exp:
P → R ≡ ¬P ∨ R (implication ki definition).
(C) me dono sides me sirf yahi substitution hai, same quantifiers => hamesha equivalent => tautology.
(A): ∀x∃y → ∃y∀x hamesha true nahi (sirf reverse direction valid).
Official key ke hisaab se (C) hi tautology hai.
Trap: (D) bhi valid lagta hai (variables rename), par key ne (C) ko answer maana.
Answer: (C)

q: Which one of the following assertions concerning code inspection and code walkthrough is true?
opts: Code inspection is carried out once the code has been unit tested
Code inspection and code walkthrough are synonyms
Adherence to coding standards is checked during code inspection
Code walkthrough is usually carried out by an independent test team
exp:
Code inspection me code ko common errors ki checklist aur coding standards ke against check kiya jaata hai.
Inspection/walkthrough unit testing se pehle hote hain (A galat).
Dono alag techniques hain (B galat).
Walkthrough development team members karte hain, independent test team nahi (D galat).
Answer: (C)

q: A half adder is implemented with XOR and AND gates. A full adder is implemented with two half adders and one OR gate. The propagation delay of an XOR gate is twice that of an AND/OR gate. The propagation delay of an AND/OR gate is 1.2 microseconds. A 4-bit ripple-carry binary adder is implemented by using four full adders. The total propagation time of this 4-bit binary adder in microseconds is ______.
exp:
AND/OR = 1.2 µs, XOR = 2.4 µs.
Full adder ka carry path: pehle half adder ka XOR (A⊕B) = 2.4, doosre half adder ka AND = 1.2, phir OR = 1.2.
Ek full adder ki delay = 2.4 + 1.2 + 1.2 = 4.8 µs.
Ripple-carry me 4 stages series me: 4 × 4.8 = 19.2 µs.
Answer: 19.2
